flags.name: Flag 1 - CF Nav
flags.description: Go to the Cloudflare console and click Manage Account from the options on the left-hand navigation. Select Configurations from the dropdown, then click Lists from the nav bar at the top of the page. A playbook adds a malicious IP to a reusable ____ that WAF and Gateway rules can reference. The flag is what malicious IPs can be added to in this specific context.

hints.description: Look for the reusable object type under <s1-label>Lists</s1-label>.
The flag is <s1-answer>IP List</s1-answer>

flags.name: Flag 2 - CF Nav
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, click Domains from the left-hand navigation and select the one-flare.com zone. From that domain's Overview page, open the Security dropdown in the left-hand menu and choose Security Rules. What is the name of a Custom Rule a SOAR playbook could toggle to block an attacker? The flag is the name of the Custom Rule in place that can block an attacker.

hints.description: The flag is in the custom-rules list.
The flag is the only security rule for <s1-value>one-flare.com</s1-value> that has the <s1-value>block</s1-value> action enabled.
The flag is <s1-answer>Mitigate definite bot traffic</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 3 - Analytics
flags.description: Open Cloudflare's documentation on the WAF attack score at https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/about/waf-attack-score/ and read how the numeric scale is calculated and what the range represents. A request is scored 3 out of 99 by the WAF attack score. What does that tell you? The flag is the finding based on a score of 3.

hints.description: The scale is counter-intuitive — most people guess it backwards.
1 means the WAF is most confident it IS an attack; 99 means clean.
The flag is <s1-answer>Almost certainly an attack</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 4 - Analytics
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, click Analytics from the left-hand navigation and select HTTP Traffic from the dropdown at the top of the page. Scroll down to the Referers panel. Change the Absolute time range to see data from the last 30 days. In the context of web traffic monitoring, a Referer is the webpage that linked to the resource being requested. In other words, it is inbound traffic from a link. So if a visitor to example.com clicks a link to your site there, the request will include a Referer header saying they came via example.com. The flag is the most prevalentReferer.

hints.description: The flag is under the <s1-label>Requests by volume source</s1-label> section of the page, under <s1-label>Referers</s1-label>.
The store front is 'shop'; the employee portal is 'portal'; the REST gateway is 'api'.
The flag is <s1-answer>shop.soledrop.co</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 5 - Soledrop
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Open a new browser tab and navigate to <s1-value>https://shop.soledrop.co/status</s1-value> to view the store's public status page.</s1-nav>

The store is publishing an active incident. What is the operation called?
 
<s1-flag example="50">The flag is the name of the operation <s1-value>shop.soledrop.co</s1-value> is under attack by.</s1-value></s1-flag>

hints.description: The banner names the operation currently hitting the store.
Two words after the hyphenated day name — it is a swarm of something automated.
The flag is <s1-answer>Drop-Day Bot Swarm</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 6 - Bot score
flags.description: Open Cloudflare's bot score documentation at http://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot-score/ and read the Bot Groupings subsection to see how score ranges map to bot-likelihood bands. Cloudflare uses Bot Scores to measure the likelihood that an incoming web request is operated by an automated bot rather than a human. A bot score of 1 indicates the highest probability of bot activity, while a bot score of 99 indicates human activity. The flag is the band a bot score of 24 would fall into.

hints.description: Scores 30-99 are in the likely human band. The flag is the band covering scores 2-29.
The flag is <s1-answer>Likely automated</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 7 - Logpush
flags.description: Open Cloudflare's Logpush documentation at https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/ and review the list of available datasets Logpush can export. Logpush allows Cloudflare to send large volumes of specified traffic logs to storage services, log management providers and SIEMs like SentinelOne. Which dataset carries WAF block and challenge decisions, separately from the HTTP request log? The flag is the name of the dataset.

hints.description: HTTP request logs record every request. Security decisions, Load balancing, and Workers are different datasets.
The flag is <s1-answer>Firewall</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 8 - Default time
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Event Search from the left-hand menu. Without changing anything, look at the time-range dropdown next to the purple Search button to see its default value. The lookback window is the period of time Event Search will look back on and show logs for. A time of 24 hours means that Event Search will show you results for anything matching your query, but only from within the past 24 hours. The flag is the default time range for Event Search.

hints.description: The format for the time range is 'Last __ days/hours/minutes'
It is measured in hours, and it is a single digit.
The flag is <s1-answer>4 hours</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 9 - Data ingest
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Event Search. Clear any existing query and set the time range to the last 72 hours. Open the field browser, filter on dataSource.vendor, select Cloudflare, and click into dataSource.cloudflare_dataset to see the values it holds. With Logpush enabled, Cloudflare can send all the relevant logs to the SentinelOne console for triage and response. Logpush can be configured to handle all sorts of volumes to fit the specific needs of your SOC team. The flag is the approximate number of logs coming from Cloudflare.

hints.description: After finding the dataVender.source field, clicking on it will show the number of logs coming from SentinelOne internally, and Cloudflare externally.
The flag is <s1-answer>100,000</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 10 - Detection
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Detections from the left-hand menu. Find the detection rule for Credential Stuffing and open it. Detections are a feature of SentinelOne that allow you to create queries that are applied to all incoming traffic. If a log or set of logs match the pattern they are aggregated into an alert for the SOC team to analyze. Find the detection associated with Credential Stuffing. The flag is the Rule Type associated with this detection.

hints.description: In the detection rule, scroll down to find the <s1-label>Detection logic conditions</s1-label> subsection which contains the <s1-label>Rule Type</s1-label>.
The flag is <s1-answer>Scheduled</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 11 - Detection
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Detections, open the Credential Stuffing rule, and read the filter status in (...) line of its scheduled PowerQuery body. PowerQuery in SentinelOne (also referred to as S1QL 2.0) is an advanced query interface designed for the Singularity XDR and SentinelOne Data Lake platforms. Originally derived from SentinelOne's DataSet (formerly Scalyr) engine, PowerQuery goes beyond simple keyword filtering to allow security teams to transform, manipulate, group, and summarize vast amounts of telemetry data on the fly. The rule only counts login requests that failed. Which set of HTTP status codes does its query treat as a failed login? The flag is the error code or codes.

hints.description: The query has a <s1-value>filter status in (...)</s1-value> line — read it literally.
Unauthorized and Forbidden are two of the three. The third is a rate-limit code.
The flag is <s1-answer>401, 403, 429</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 12 - Detection
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Detections from the left-hand menu. Find the rule whose name contains CF-WAF-Traversal and open it. What severity is this detection rule configured with? The flag is the severity level.

hints.description: Read the <s1-label>Severity</s1-label> field on the rule itself, not the alert.
It is one step below <s1-value>Critical</s1-value>.
The flag is <s1-answer>High</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 13 - CF Filtering
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, navigate to Zero Trust from the left-hand menu. Navigate to the Traffic Policies from the new left-hand menu and select Traffic Settings from the dropdown. Scroll down to the Traffic Logging section. Cloudflare allows users to configure what events actually get logged. What is the default scope that Gateway uses when capturing events? The flag is the default scope.

hints.description: It is the most permissive of the options.
The flag is <s1-answer>Capture all</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 14 - Event Search Evidence
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Detections and open the Bulk Data Exfiltration rule (CF-API-Exfil). Read the filter line at the end of its PowerQuery body. This rule fires on either of two conditions. One of them is a response-size floor — a single response body larger than N bytes. What is N? The flag is the string + domain that is cited as evidence.

hints.description: The query ends with <s1-value>filter sensitive_hits >= 10 OR max_bytes >= N</s1-value>.
It is one binary megabyte, written out in full.
The flag is <s1-answer>1048576</s1-answer>.
